newsitem.title: USA: Kasich sees no U.S. government shutdown on budget.
newsitem.headline: Kasich sees no U.S. government shutdown on budget.

text.p: House Budget Committee chairman John Kasich said there would be no government shutdown, as there was last year, if Capitol Hill Republicans and President Clinton fail to agree on a federal spending plan this year.
"The government is not going to close down again," Kasich, an Ohio Republican, told reporters after a meeting with other congressional budget committee leaders and Clinton at the White House.
If no agreement is reached, Congress would allow agencies to continue operating at the same spending levels, he said.
"If in fact we can't reach any agreement, we would basically say that in these areas, we would spend no more than last year, we would freeze spending," Kasich said.

He said the discussion with Clinton was "candid" but declined to give details, saying there would be more contacts between White House officials and congressional Republicans and their staffs in the coming weeks. "I choose not to characterize the discussion as good or bad," he said. "We're going to keep talking."
Senate Budget Committee chairman Pete Domenici, Republican of New Mexico, said Republicans would work seriously to narrow the gap on budget ideas, including during the upcoming congressional recess.
"We agreed to work ... to narrow our differences. It is very clear there are big differences," Domenici said. He and Kasich spoke to reporters outside the White House.

Democrats who attended the meeting described it as a general session but said they thought it was good it had been held. "No one was willing to throw out the first card on the table," said Sen. Frank Lautenberg, a New Jersey Demcocrat.
